description: Formally repeat the explored committed-removal history, observing voter eligibility and fresh support at a subsequent ReadOnlySafe call; compare automatic stepdown enabled/disabled.

harness.description: Two public RawNode histories with actual elections, committed removal application, later write application and removed-node read invocation.
semantic_changes: MemoryStorage and deterministic ordered workers implement caller duties.
Caller continues invoking the removed RawNode; external service shutdown is not modeled.

legality.derivation: Initialize two RawNodes through public Storage snapshot/HardState methods, actually campaign node 1, propose ConfChangeRemoveNode(1), and invoke ApplyConfChange only from actual MsgStorageApply committed entries. Both nodes must report sole voter 2. Campaign node 2 and propose a distinct write; record its actual application before invoking removed node ReadIndex. StepDownOnRemoval is the only paired variant. No roles, terms, commit positions or membership maps are assigned directly. Async append and application workers run FIFO and return responses after their work. A read request is issued once and all available work drains regardless of whether it emits a ReadState.
legality.applicability: No clocks or network loss are needed after the committed removal; node 2 does not send protocol traffic to removed node 1 under its installed config. Caller keeps the RawNode alive, which is the exact library API scope rather than an assumed deployment routing policy. MemoryStorage substitutes for caller persistence; callback application is recorded before response. No crash or client read return is modeled.
unresolved: External shutdown/routing mitigations are not tested.
alternatives: StepDownOnRemoval=true is exercised without requiring a ReadState or treating silence as a violation.

grounding.derivation: before_read is emitted after real committed removal and later write application, before invoking ReadIndex. after_read is emitted after that synchronous API call returns and all generated protocol work drains. Operation identity is step_down (the two independent executions). eligible_support is measured from the current voter membership and authentic newly delivered heartbeat/read-index responses from voter 2 with the request context; both raw components are also emitted. released is count of actual matching Ready.ReadStates > 0. The necessity implication compares output only when eligible_support is false. No-output control completes the API observation interval without claiming a completed client read or owed liveness. write_index/read_index remain raw context and are not the oracle.
grounding.applicability: Active configuration is verified to contain only voter 2 before request, no later config change occurs, and every delivered message is logged by the deterministic transport. Identity does not filter on the compared output or support. The two subtests are independent, not combined into one protocol history.
unresolved: This is a library ReadState release comparison, not a client state-machine result.
alternatives: An integration can avoid calling ReadIndex after removal; this does not alter the tested library output.

observable_properties.description: Without local voter eligibility or fresh sole-voter support, no safe ReadState may be released; no-output is permitted.

uncertainties: No external application client return is measured.
Continued invocation on removed RawNode is the explicit library scope; integration shutdown mitigations are excluded.
